take: Brent tumbled 5% to $91 this week even as tankers are hit daily, because recovering Gulf flows and a looming surplus are outweighing geopolitical risk, and the EIA's 19% third-quarter increase in Middle East chokepoint shipments underscores that supply is moving rather than being strangled. The macro cross-current is a violent risk-off in US tech—the Nasdaq's worst week since 2020 and a $2.3 trillion chip wipeout—which threatens demand sentiment and paper length across the energy complex, whilst Trump's consideration of new Iran strikes cuts the other way and keeps a geopolitical bid lurking under the surface. On positioning, the third straight weekly decline in crude tells you the market is trading the glut narrative, and the distillate-heavy refinery yield shift plus Lufthansa cutting up to 1,000 jobs on high fuel costs flags jet and middle-distillate demand destruction that could soften the products crack. Watch the gasoil-bunker and distillate cracks against the flat price—if middle distillates hold whilst crude slides, the refinery yield shift is doing real work and the products complex is the cleaner short. In the next 24 hours, watch for any escalation or de-escalation on Iran strikes, the follow-through in Asian equity and FX markets at the Monday open, and whether the rig count rising into falling prices starts to bend the US supply narrative.
